title: Insulin Dosing Protocol for Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes
author: Verbueken, Yuan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Expansion Medium
steps.instruction: Mix 49 mL RPMI‑1640 (1×) with 1 mL B‑27 supplement (50×, serum‑free). Add CHIR‑99021 to a final concentration of 2–4 µM (10–20 µL of 10 mM stock). Optionally add 1 % Penicillin/Streptomycin. Store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature (20 °C) for ≥30 min before use. Note: optimal CHIR‑99021 concentration may vary by cell line; test a range to identify the most effective dose.

steps.title: Optional Purification Before Expansion
steps.instruction: If culture purity is <80 %, perform metabolic selection before expansion.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the existing culture medium from each well.
Add 2 mL Purification Medium A to each well.
Incubate for 48 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.
Re‑assess purity; repeat the sub‑steps if purity remains <80 % (total purification time may reach 96 h).

steps.title: Expand hiPSC‑CMs
steps.instruction: Replace the medium with the prepared Expansion Medium and culture the cells according to your experimental schedule.

steps.title: Optional Purification Before Maturation
steps.instruction: If purity is still <80 % after expansion, perform a second metabolic selection before maturation.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the existing culture medium from each well.
Add 2 mL Purification Medium B to each well (see Materials and Equipment).
Incubate for 48 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.
Re‑assess purity; repeat the sub‑steps if purity remains <80 % (total purification time may reach 96 h).

steps.title: Prepare No‑Insulin Maturation Medium
steps.instruction: Mix 49 mL RPMI‑1640 (1×) with 1 mL B‑27 supplement (50×) that lacks insulin. Optionally add 1 % Penicillin/Streptomycin. Store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature (20 °C) for ≥30 min before use.

steps.title: Prepare Low‑Dose Insulin Medium
steps.instruction: Mix 50 mL RPMI‑1640 (1×) with 900 µL B‑27 supplement (50×) minus insulin (0.9×) and 100 µL B‑27 supplement (50×) serum‑free (0.1×). Optionally add 1 % Penicillin/Streptomycin. Store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature (20 °C) for ≥30 min before use.

steps.title: Mature hiPSC‑CMs
steps.instruction: Replace the medium with the chosen maturation medium (either No‑Insulin or Low‑Dose Insulin) and culture the cells under standard conditions (37 °C, 5 % CO₂).

description: Since the discovery of the Yamanaka factors to induce pluripotent stem cells from human somatic cells, various approaches have been established to differentiate human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into cardiomyocytes. Lian et al.2 showed that through chemical stage-specific modulation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in RPMI/B27 Medium, highly pure cultures of hiPSC-CMs can be obtained (80–98% cTnT+). An overview of the different protocols and their evolution over time is summarized elsewhere.3 Using this RPMI/B27-directed differentiation approach, re-activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway in immature hiPSC-CMs was shown to induce massive expansion, yielding a ∼250-fold increase in cell number over 3–5 passages.4 Recently, we have shown that the high insulin concentration in the B27+ Supplement (∼58 nM, 340 ng/mL) is required for this massive proliferative response via activation of the IGF–AKT–FOXO axis.1 Removal of insulin, by using B27- supplement, blunted the increase in hiPSC-CMs that are actively engaging in the cell cycle upon Wnt/β-catenin activation from 25- to 5-fold. Removal of both insulin and Wnt/β-catenin activation led to rapid cell cycle exit, increased RNA expression of mature sarcomeric isotypes, and enhanced sarcomeric and mitochondrial organization. Low concentrations of insulin (∼10 nM) already facilitate the translocation of GLUT4 towards the membrane in cardiac myocytes.5 Using a 1 in 10 mix of the B27+ and B27- supplement (1:10 B27+/B27-, ∼5.8 nM) we show that the metabolism of hiPSC-CMs is enhanced without activating the cell cycle via the IGF–AKT–FOXO axis. In this protocol we provide an easy and cost-effective strategy for hiPSC-CM differentiation and control of resulting hiPSC-CM cell fate through modulation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and insulin dosing, and offer practical recommendations through hands-on experience.
